rv.q: Each member of the 14-strong cast can sing, dance, act and play a musical instrument and do justice to the plentiful songs that are rooted in indie folk of Broderick’s Kentish group.
Franz & Marie is on much firmer ground when director Michael Oakley leans into the tragedy of the piece; as it stands, the comedy is just too flimsy and gets in the way of the dark story.
With an incredibly talented cast, atmospheric live music and a story that stays with you long after the curtain falls, this is a production that deserves to be experienced.
Overall, this powerful portrayal of intense themes is well worth a watch, as the audience is transported to an eerie world through excellent storytelling and a first-class cast.
The outcome is a deeply talented cast transitioning seamlessly from delivering dialogue to performing Rob Shepherd and Chris Broderick’s music with aplomb.
Franz & Marie is an ambitious and atmospheric production that successfully combines a tragic story with a distinctive folk-inspired musical style.
Although it needs some tightening, this folk musical is a disturbing yet toe-stomping night at the theatre.
There is so much happening in this quirky and hugely entertaining production.
If the script and lyrics let the production down, the musical numbers – delivered with passion – manage to lift it back up again.

cn.t: Critics are divided on this folk musical adaptation of Büchner's Woyzeck, with reactions ranging from "horrendously bad" to "hugely entertaining." Strong performances and ambitious staging earn praise, but some find it tuneless and misguided.
